note: The Polaris verification conformance cases. Each case names the `artifact` it is about (default `authenticity-pack`), references a published vector, and states the verdict a conformant verifier MUST return; the runner checks every key the case constrains. `anchors: "self"` means the pack's own public key is trusted; `now` pins the evaluation time for a windowed artifact. See SPEC.md and docs/reference/WIRE-SPEC.md. Each case carries `since`, the protocol release that introduced it: a verifier pinned at an older release MUST agree on every case at or before its release and MUST NOT accept anything a later case expects rejected (the cross-version rule, wire spec section 6).

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: revocation-feed-fresh

cases.name: revocation-feed-commitment-mismatch
cases.note: v9.432: a feed whose signature is genuine and whose commitment is a lie. Its only refusal case tampered the SIGNATURE and left commitment_ok true, so nothing published exercised the commitment at all: a verifier that never recomputed the revoked root conformed, and an authority could sign one root while publishing different leaves.

cases.note: 2026-09-27: a presentation that states no context is not decided under an edge from any context. Before this every verifier treated a missing context as a wildcard, so a relying party reading the context from the presentation accepted one that left it out.

cases.name: id-token-wrong-audience
cases.note: the SAME valid token, offered to a different relying party. Its signature is perfectly good; accepting it is audience confusion. A verifier that checks only the signature passes every other case in this suite and fails here.

cases.name: id-token-wrong-nonce
cases.note: the right relying party, the wrong login. The nonce binds the token to ONE authentication; without it a token captured from an earlier login is replayable.

cases.name: id-token-expired
cases.note: authentic and expired are different answers. The signature stays good forever; the window does not.

cases.name: id-token-accepted-by-its-own-relying-party
cases.note: the positive control for the three above: without it a verifier that answered False to every question would pass them all.

cases.name: id-token-trusted-issuer

cases.name: pack-mldsa87-valid
cases.note: P8.8a: a genuine ML-DSA-87 pack verifies; an accepted parameter set beside the default.

cases.name: pack-mldsa87-tampered
cases.note: P8.8a: one flipped signature byte under ML-DSA-87.

cases.name: pack-mldsa44-unaccepted
cases.note: P8.8a: a GENUINE ML-DSA-44 signature MUST be refused: the parameter set is below the floor (wire spec section 6).

cases.name: status-assertion-mldsa87-active
cases.note: P8.8a: the status assertion under ML-DSA-87.

cases.name: trust-list-migration
cases.note: P8.8a: an algorithm migration recorded in a trust list: the ML-DSA-65 key retired, the ML-DSA-87 key active and signing.

cases.name: trust-list-migration-retired-signer
cases.note: P8.8a: the same list signed by the RETIRED ML-DSA-65 key is refused: a publisher signs only under a key it lists active.

cases.name: exchange-receipt-valid
cases.note: P8.2: the responder-signed receipt a service holds after an exchange; evidence without the payload.

cases.name: exchange-receipt-tampered
cases.note: P8.2: the response commitment changed after signing.

cases.name: exchange-mint-valid
cases.note: P8.2b: the statement a responder's service signs to mint a receipt; `algorithm` rides unsigned.

cases.name: exchange-mint-tampered
cases.note: P8.2b: the responder agency changed after signing.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-valid
cases.note: P9.6: the inclusion proof reconstructs a head the expected log key signed.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-witnessed
cases.note: P9.6: two distinct trusted witnesses have cosigned this exact head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-unwitnessed
cases.note: P9.6: anchored, but nobody the verifier trusts has cosigned the head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-forged-head
cases.note: P9.6: a stolen log key can sign a fabricated head; it cannot make a trusted witness cosign it.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-broken-proof
cases.note: P9.6: the path does not reconstruct the head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-forged-cosignature
cases.note: both cosigners are trusted and one of the two signatures is forged, so the threshold of two is not met. Counting a cosignature without verifying it makes the witness quorum arithmetic rather than evidence.

cases.name: trust-attestation-valid
cases.note: P9.5: the attesting agency signed this edge itself; it is not the operator's word.

cases.name: trust-attestation-rekeyed
cases.note: P9.5: the edge is bound to the attested KEY, so re-pointing it at another key breaks it.

cases.name: trust-attestation-widened
cases.note: P9.5: the context is signed, so an edge cannot be widened after the fact.

cases.name: trust-attestation-from-another-agency
cases.note: the SAME valid attestation, offered as though agency 3 had signed it. The signature is good; it is simply not from the agency the relying party is asking about. A verifier that checks only the signature accepts it.

cases.name: trust-attestation-for-another-key
cases.note: the attestation is genuine and it attests a DIFFERENT key than the one being relied on. The edge has to bind to the key actually in hand.

cases.name: trust-attestation-accepted-for-its-own-agency-and-key
cases.note: the positive control for the two above: without it a verifier that refused every attestation would pass them both.

cases.name: holder-binding-valid
cases.note: P9.1: the issuer's signed statement that this holder key belongs to this credential.

cases.name: holder-binding-tampered
cases.note: P9.1: the bound key was swapped after signing.

cases.name: holder-binding-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.note: v9.431: the same genuine artifact, read by a relying party who trusts the key that signed it.

cases.name: holder-proof-valid
cases.note: P9.1: the holder's own signature over the credential, context, nonce and instant.

cases.name: holder-proof-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: holder-proof had one case and it expected authentic: true. The holder-chain refusals each fail for a non-signature reason (a stranger's key, a replayed nonce, a revoked binding), so forcing the signature check permissive left every case green.

cases.name: holder-proof-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: holder-chain-proved
cases.note: P9.1: the party presenting the credential holds the key its issuer bound to it.

cases.name: holder-chain-stranger
cases.note: P9.1: a genuine proof by a key the issuer never bound proves nothing about this credential.

cases.name: holder-chain-replayed
cases.note: P9.1: a proof naming another verifier's nonce is a replay of one made for somebody else.

cases.name: holder-chain-revoked
cases.note: P9.1: a revoked binding means the holder has no usable key until a new one is bound.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-valid
cases.note: P9.2: the published anonymity set, signed, with the leaves committed by leaves_root_hex.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-swapped
cases.note: P9.2: a member swapped after signing; the commitment no longer matches the set.

cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: agent-grant-valid
cases.note: P9.8: a holder-signed grant naming its actions, limits and expiry.

cases.name: agent-grant-widened
cases.note: P9.8: an action was added after signing. actions is inside the signed statement precisely so this fails.

cases.name: agent-grant-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: agent-grant-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: grant-revocation-valid
cases.note: P9.8: the holder ends the grant with the same key that signed it. The issuer is not contacted and the human's credential is untouched.

cases.name: grant-revocation-impostor
cases.note: P9.8: the SIGNATURE is genuine, but by a key that is not the grant's holder. A verifier must check that binding separately: authenticity alone does not end a grant, or anyone able to publish bytes could revoke somebody else's.

cases.name: grant-revocation-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: as for agent-proof. A revocation whose signature nobody verifies is a revocation anyone can mint, which ends a grant that is still valid.

cases.name: agent-proof-valid
cases.note: P9.8: the agent's signature over the grant, the action and the service's nonce.

cases.name: agent-proof-impostor
cases.note: P9.8: genuinely signed, by a key the grant does not name. Without the key-matches-grant check a copied grant would be a bearer token.

cases.name: agent-proof-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: every published agent-proof case expected authentic: true, including the impostor one (a genuine signature by the wrong key is authentic and powerless). So no case exercised the signature at all, and a verifier that never checked it conformed.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-widened-grant
cases.note: An action added to the grant after signing. A grant the holder did not sign grants nothing, so its scope is not read at all: answering from the forged list would honour the forger's own action.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-in-scope
cases.note: The requested action is in the grant's signed scope.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-out-of-scope
cases.note: A genuine grant used for an action it does not name. Authenticity is not permission.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revoked-by-holder
cases.note: The holder's own revocation of this grant ends it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revocation-by-impostor
cases.note: A genuinely signed revocation by a key that is not the grant's holder ends nothing; otherwise anyone able to publish bytes could revoke somebody else's grant.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-agent-proved
cases.note: The agent proves it holds the key the grant names, for this action and this nonce.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-by-impostor
cases.note: A genuine proof by a key the grant does not name: a copied grant is not a bearer token.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-replayed
cases.note: The agent's genuine proof, presented to a service that issued a different nonce: a replay.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-bound
cases.note: The grant is signed by the key the credential's issuer bound to the holder, under an active binding. The verifier's handle for this principal is pairwise, and still a stable value it can store: correlation is exposed, not bounded.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-binding-revoked
cases.note: The issuer revoked the holder's binding (a lost device). A grant signed with that key speaks for nobody: a revoked binding means the holder has no usable key.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-stranger
cases.note: A genuine grant signed by a key no issuer bound to this credential.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-binding-wrong-type
cases.note: A genuinely issuer-signed object of ANOTHER type, carrying a binding's fields outside what that type signs. Only its format says it is not a binding.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-authorized
cases.note: The envelope is by the requester expected, attested in its context by a trusted authority whose manifest is fresh at `now`, and the body held is the one it commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-other-requester
cases.note: A genuine envelope from a requester other than the one this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-context-not-attested
cases.note: The requester is attested in context 1, and this envelope is for context 3. Trust is in-context.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-forged-manifest
cases.note: The only attestation for context 3 was added to the manifest after the authority signed it, so the authority never said it.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-attestation-expired
cases.note: The requester's attestation in context 2 closed an hour before `now`; the manifest carrying it is still fresh, and the attestation's own window decides.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-manifest-stale
cases.note: The same envelope and manifest, decided at an instant after the manifest expired. The decision is made at the stated `now`, not at whatever the verifier's clock says.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-other-body
cases.note: A body other than the one the envelope's request_hash commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-stranger-signed
cases.note: A genuine signature by a stranger's key over an envelope naming the requester: the key that verifies must be the requester the signed statement claims. An envelope that is not the requester's answers nothing further.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing. A forged envelope answers nothing further.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-authorized
cases.note: The receipt is by the responder expected; a trusted authority attests the requester in the receipt's context (`via` names it); both bodies, as exchanged, match the commitments; and it names the responder it was signed by.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-other-responder
cases.note: A genuine receipt from a responder other than the one this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-context-not-attested
cases.note: The requester is attested in context 1, and this receipt is for context 3.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-no-context
cases.note: A genuinely signed receipt that states no context, beside a fresh trusted manifest attesting the requester in context 1. Attested in the receipt's context means that context exactly: before 1.0.0-rc.64 the detached verifier accepted an attestation from ANY context here.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-nameless-authority
cases.note: A genuine, fresh manifest attests the requester in the receipt's context but names no authority. A receipt's authorization answers BY WHOM (`via`), and a manifest that names nobody cannot be that answer.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-manifest-stale
cases.note: The same receipt and manifest, decided after the manifest expired.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-other-bodies
cases.note: Bodies other than the ones the receipt commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-body-reserialized
cases.note: The same request re-serialized with whitespace. A receipt commits to the body bytes as exchanged, so a verifier hashes the body as given and does not re-serialize it.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing. A forged receipt answers nothing further, and names no responder: its `responder` field is the forger's word.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-responder-matches
cases.note: The mint statement is signed by the responder expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-other-responder
cases.note: A genuine mint statement by a key other than the responder this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing; a forged mint answers nothing further.

cases.name: transplant-manifest-genuine
cases.note: The artifact whose signature the next case moves: a genuine manifest by the transplant authority.

cases.name: pack-transplanted-artifact-signature
cases.note: The manifest's genuine signature and canonical statement, wrapped as a pack, with its key trusted. A pack's token_value MUST be a credential serial (WIRE-SPEC 3.7): every other artifact signs a JSON statement, which begins with '{'. Before 1.0.0-rc.64 every shipped verifier reported this authentic and its issuer trusted.

cases.name: pack-transplant-control-valid
cases.note: Control: the same authority's key over a credential serial verifies and is trusted, so the refusal above is the serial rule's and not the key's.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-signed-open
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: the edge is signed and its own window is open at now: the positive control.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-signed-closed
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: the edge is signed and its own window closed a month before now; the manifest is fresh.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-unsigned-open
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: a legacy edge states a window that is open at now: the positive control.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-unsigned-closed
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: a legacy edge states a window that closed before now: the manifest's authority signed that window, and a fresh manifest does not extend an edge its authority has ended.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-base
cases.note: The positive control: the genuine setup every variant below differs from in one fact.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-clean
cases.note: The positive control for the feed variants: an authentic, fresh feed from the issuer that revokes nothing.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-manifest-stale
cases.note: A manifest past its own window confers nothing, however genuine.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-attestation-other-key
cases.note: An edge that attests another key does not attest this credential's issuer.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-attestation-bad-signature
cases.note: A present-but-invalid edge signature refuses the edge (wire spec section 3.14).

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-retired-anchor
cases.note: Trusting only a key the manifest lists as RETIRED confers no trust in it.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-stale
cases.note: A supplied feed must be fresh (wire spec section 4, item 3): fail-closed.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-other-issuer
cases.note: A supplied feed must be bound to the issuer's key: another authority's word about this credential is not the issuer's.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-not-authentic
cases.note: A supplied feed must be authentic: a forged or altered one rejects.
